text:
cameron: Heads-up — saw a cluster-autoscaler-triggered GPU downscale in us-west-2 at 09:03 that looks like noise from our heartbeat aggregation. Warm-pool nodes were marked idle even though KV cache rehydration happened within 30s.
priya: Ugh, saw the same. Latency spike for prod-chat for ~45s. Cost saved but upcall failures for a few tenants.
zhang: Can you paste the autoscaler event?
ops-bot: [event] cluster-autoscaler: ScaleDown: node/warmpool-usw2-7 marked for deletion (low utilization). cpuUtil: 2.9%, gpuUtil: <3%, lastSeen: 10m
cameron: Here — autoscaler uses a 10m inactivity window + simple moving average of gpu_util. The problem: our tiny bursts (cache replays) are 20-40s, below the window. Jitter in the heartbeat stream (kubelet probes) is causing undercounting.
lee: Do we have any PDBs or disruption exemptions on warmpool pods? I thought warm-pool-control-plane had a toleration to avoid scale-to-zero.
marta: Not uniformly. Some warmpool-managed pods are pure infra and have no PDB. Nodecontroller removes them as soon as they hit the idle threshold.
priya: Proposal: add a "redwood.com/keep-warm=true" label on nodes we want excluded from aggressive downscale + increase heartbeat smoothing for GPU metrics to a 3-bucket median instead of SMA.
zhang: SGTM. Also add an allowlist for pod names that are KV cache holders: rdb-kvcache-*, prefix-cache-* so bursts don't count as idle.
cameron: Quick config patch I tested locally that avoids immediate eviction for nodes with the label:
```
kubectl patch node warmpool-usw2-7 -p '{"metadata": {"labels": {"redwood.com/keep-warm": "true"}}}'
```
Works but needs automation in nodepool controller.
lee: Longer term we should change cluster-autoscaler to consider a weighted signal: if node had any GPU activity in last 3m (even if average < threshold) mark as keep for extra cooldown interval. That would reduce churn.
marta: We also need better telemetry to prove cost impact. My rough numbers: 18% over-downscale => ~ $18k/month extra because we then spin up more dedicated pods and pay burst premium.
priya: For immediate mitigation I'll open a PR to: 1) label warm-pool nodes on creation, 2) bump scale-down-window to 15m for those pools, 3) add kvcache allowlist.
zhang: Can we instead toggle the node taint: `redwood.com/warmpool=reserved:NoSchedule` and only allow the warm pool controller to tolerate it? That way normal CA won't evict them unless explicitly allowed.
cameron: That might block legitimate autoscaling when we need to reclaim GPUs for higher-priority workloads. Prefer label + CAS policy.
lee: If we do the label route, also add a small controller that auto-annotates nodes with last-gpu-burst timestamp. Then cluster-autoscaler can consult the annotation.
priya: I'm drafting the PR now. Will include these snippets and a link to the test harness: https://git.redwood/repo/warmpool-sim — includes a sim showing reduced thundering by ~70%.
marta: FYI, cost team wants a rollback plan if reserved labels lead to persistent waste. Add a nightly job that checks warm node idle fraction and auto-cleans labels if > 50% idle over 24h.
zhang: Nice safety net. Also add a metric: `redwood.warmpool.keep_warm_effective` and an alert if >5% of traffic sees >2x coldstart.
lee: I'm +1 on immediate label patch + autoscaler consult via annotation. Will review PR.
ops-bot: Scheduled: warmpool-label-rollout at 01:30 UTC in canary region (us-west-2-canary).
cameron: Thanks — will watch canary and report results.
priya: ping me if you see any spike, I'll rollback the label en masse. :thumbsup:
